William & Mary & Wawa

Consumers love the results of free enterprise.

By

If you wanted to point to a single place in the United States that was most influential in the intellectual creation of American liberty and law, you could make a strong case for the Williamsburg, Va., campus of William & Mary. Now from the esteemed university comes a new lesson about the value of freedom and consumer choice.

On Tuesday this column noted the latest failure of a government-backed supermarket that didn’t meet the needs of customers. Today brings news of a private market so beloved by customers that many are demanding it remain open forever. James Robinson reports for the Virginian-Pilot:
